Image to GLB
Turn a clean reference image into a checked 3D asset.

Start with one focused object in the Img3D image to 3D workflow, generate a GLB, then inspect orientation, scale, and material loading in the Img3D local viewer.

Public generation status appears here. Local file inspection has its own viewer results.
Tool guides
Img3D GLB viewer: open GLB and glTF files in the browser and read the bounding box, estimated vertex count, and file size.
Img3D image to 3D: how the free image to GLB generator runs, which source images work, and how the daily allowance is spent.
Img3D image to 3D model: what a generated model carries, and the checks to run before importing it into an engine or a slicer.
Img3D STL viewer: check an STL bounding box and triangle estimate before slicing, and resize the model for printing.
Input and output formats
Generator input: PNG, JPG, WebP, or AVIF up to 4 MB, or a public image link. The image to 3D guide shows which source images survive the trip to 3D.
Generator output: one GLB file. The image to 3D model guide lists what the file carries and the export path to OBJ, FBX, STL, PLY, glTF, or USDZ.
Local viewer input: GLB, glTF, OBJ, STL, PLY, FBX, or 3MF, opened in the browser without an upload.
GLB, STL, or OBJ: which one do you need?

Pick GLB for web scenes, AR, and game engines: geometry, materials, and textures travel in one file, and the GLB viewer opens it. Pick STL for slicers and 3D printing: it holds triangles only, with no color and no units, so check the size in the STL viewer before printing. OBJ is an older exchange format for modeling tools: geometry first, with materials in a separate file.

Photo to 3D models: when the input is a photo of a person, a pet, or a product and you want a hosted editor instead of a browser-local check, our sibling site Photo3D runs the photo to 3D pipeline.

Img3D keeps generation, local inspection, conversion planning, source image prep, and handoff checks in the same tabbed workspace. Img3D workspace tools keep files local when the task does not need AI generation.

Start Free
1
Can Img3D inspect files locally?

Yes. Img3D workspace tools keep files local for model viewing, texture checks, image conversion, scale calculation, and handoff analysis.

2
Which source images work best?

Use one clear object, visible edges, even light, and a simple background. That gives Img3D stronger shape cues before GLB inspection.

3
What happens after generation?

Open the generated model in the Img3D viewer, check scale and materials, then choose the Img3D converter, image, PDF, or video tool needed for handoff.

4
How should commercial work be handled?

Keep rights clear for source images, generated assets, brand marks, and client files before using Img3D output in games, ads, products, or marketplaces.

5
Is Img3D image to 3D generation free?

Yes. The viewer, converter planning, texture, scale, and image tools are free and uncapped because they run in your browser. AI generation is free up to a daily allowance on a shared GPU. No account or card is needed. The shared GPU provider currently rejects the final GLB export step, so a generation run can end with an error and no file.

6
Which image formats can I upload to the generator?

PNG, JPG, WebP, or AVIF files up to 4 MB, or a public image link. Resize a larger photo in the Image Tools workspace first.

7
What file does the image to 3D generator return?

A single GLB file with the generated geometry and a material written from your source image. Open it in the GLB viewer to read the bounding box, estimated vertex count, and file size. The shared GPU provider currently rejects the final GLB export step, so a generation run can end with an error and no file.

8
Can I 3D print a model generated from an image?

Slicers read STL, so plan the route from the GLB to STL in the converter workspace, then check the bounding box and resize it in the STL viewer. A single image cannot show the back of an object, so the mesh is not guaranteed watertight. Treat it as a starting shape and finish it in a modeling tool.

GLB, STL, or OBJ: which one do you need?

Pick GLB for web scenes, AR, and game engines: geometry, materials, and textures travel in one file, and the GLB viewer opens it. Pick STL for slicers and 3D printing: it holds triangles only, with no color and no units, so check the size in the STL viewer before printing. OBJ is an older exchange format for modeling tools: geometry first, with materials in a separate file.

Photo to 3D models: when the input is a photo of a person, a pet, or a product and you want a hosted editor instead of a browser-local check, our sibling site Photo3D runs the photo to 3D pipeline.

Which source images work best?

Use one clear object, visible edges, even light, and a simple background. That gives Img3D stronger shape cues before GLB inspection.

How should commercial work be handled?

Keep rights clear for source images, generated assets, brand marks, and client files before using Img3D output in games, ads, products, or marketplaces.

Is Img3D image to 3D generation free?

Yes. The viewer, converter planning, texture, scale, and image tools are free and uncapped because they run in your browser. AI generation is free up to a daily allowance on a shared GPU. No account or card is needed. The shared GPU provider currently rejects the final GLB export step, so a generation run can end with an error and no file.

6
Which image formats can I upload to the generator?

PNG, JPG, WebP, or AVIF files up to 4 MB, or a public image link. Resize a larger photo in the Image Tools workspace first.

7
What file does the image to 3D generator return?

A single GLB file with the generated geometry and a material written from your source image. Open it in the GLB viewer to read the bounding box, estimated vertex count, and file size. The shared GPU provider currently rejects the final GLB export step, so a generation run can end with an error and no file.

8
Can I 3D print a model generated from an image?

Slicers read STL, so plan the route from the GLB to STL in the converter workspace, then check the bounding box and resize it in the STL viewer. A single image cannot show the back of an object, so the mesh is not guaranteed watertight. Treat it as a starting shape and finish it in a modeling tool.
